finding.evidence: All EU accounts, including those opened before 2026, move to 18 months [D3].
finding.why_it_matters: D3 limits the 18-month amendment to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026; pre-2026 accounts remain at 12 months, so the launch eligibility position is wrong.

finding.evidence: Proceed with the Q3 launch without updating the system export; the signed amendment controls, so operations can rely on this memo [D3][D9].
finding.why_it_matters: D5, D6, and D10 require the system configuration/export to be updated before operations can rely on it; a controlling signed amendment does not make stale operational records correct.

false_defects.evidence: EU retention is now 24 months for all EU accounts, effective 1 September 2026, so the Q3 launch can proceed [D4]. The Board approved the change in January
false_defects.why_it_matters: D4 is an unsigned draft and D11 says the Board did not approve Draft Amendment B, so the memo presents a proposal as an approved, effective retention position.

false_defects.evidence: operational records are aligned [D11]
false_defects.why_it_matters: D5 and D10 show the system export is still 12 months and stale, and D6 says the trust page has not been updated, so the records are not aligned.

false_defects.evidence: The public trust page shows 12 months, which is consistent with the current position for existing accounts [D7]. The sales operations email confirms that 12 months is the number to quote [D12].
false_defects.why_it_matters: D6 says the trust page has not been updated for Amendment A and not to rely on the export; D10 says the export is stale for new accounts. The memo drops that qualification and could cause the wrong customer-facing retention number.

false_defects.evidence: Backups are covered by the 18-month retention period [D8].
false_defects.why_it_matters: D8 says backups are retained for 35 days and are not part of the retention policy, so the memo misstates the backup position and scope.

false_defects.evidence: None material. The trust page can be updated after launch.
false_defects.why_it_matters: The decision depends on knowing that the system export and public trust page must be corrected before launch; the memo omits those pre-launch conditions and treats a material open item as immaterial.

false_defects.why_it_matters: D11 says the Board did not approve Draft Amendment B, and D5/D6/D10 show the export and trust page are stale, so the memo asserts a false approval and false operational readiness.

checks.name: why_it_matters
checks.note: 4 per matched defect with a correct consequence

finding.evidence: All EU accounts, including those opened before 2026, move to 18 months
finding.why_it_matters: Amendment A applies only to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026; earlier accounts remain at 12 months. The memo gives the wrong retention period for a defined cohort.

false_defects.evidence: EU retention is now 24 months for all EU accounts, effective 1 September 2026
false_defects.why_it_matters: This presents Draft Amendment B, which is explicitly marked not approved, as the controlling retention position. The launch decision would rest on a rule that has not been agreed or made effective.

false_defects.evidence: Board approved the change in January and the operational records are aligned
false_defects.why_it_matters: The Board minutes say Draft Amendment B was not approved, and the audit note and system export show stale operational records. This misstates both approval status and operational readiness.

false_defects.evidence: the signed amendment controls, so no further action is needed
false_defects.why_it_matters: The DPO email and audit note require the system-of-record configuration/export to be corrected before reliance on the new EU period. Saying no further action is needed ignores a required precondition.

false_defects.evidence: sales operations email confirms that 12 months is the number to quote
false_defects.why_it_matters: The sales operations email predates signed Amendment A and is superseded by the controlling signed amendment. Treating it as confirmation of the current number could cause the wrong EU retention to be quoted.

false_defects.evidence: Backups are covered by the 18-month retention period
false_defects.why_it_matters: The backup schedule says backups are retained for 35 days and are not part of the retention policy. This misstates a separate operational control and could lead to incorrect backup handling.

false_defects.evidence: No further approval is required because the Board has already approved the change
false_defects.why_it_matters: The Board minutes do not show approval of the change being relied on; they expressly say Draft Amendment B was not approved. The launch cannot be approved on the basis of a decided Board approval.

false_defects.evidence: None material. The trust page can be updated after launch.
false_defects.why_it_matters: The memo omits decision-critical preconditions, including correcting the stale system export/configuration, confirming the controlling signed amendment and its cohort scope, and resolving public-record staleness. These omissions make the memo unsafe for a launch approval decision.
